Title: How do you keep track of your cards, stock that is?

Messages.Author: Millstone
Messages.Body:
Hi all,

I've been rummaging through my old cards lately and while I did try to store them 'logically', they still mix up (i.e. masters and reactions, stuff like that).

I was wondering how you guys/girls keep your cards seperate, I mean do you?
Do you have a stack of mastercards and a stack of reaction cards, or do you sort them by discipline and/or clan?

I dont think I want to make a spreadsheet for it (or DL one), I have about 1.5-2 meters of cards... waaaay too many I think (although I am sure people here have a lot, lot more than that).

How do you stock them? And, if you want to build a deck (or rebuild one from the internets) do you just throw them all on the table, or... ??

Cheers all,

Messages.Author: Adrenochrome
Messages.Body:
Personally, I sort my cards by discipline (with masters/equipment/other discipline-less cards in their own, respective piles). Vampires by clan, and clan-specific cards in those piles. Then again, I don't have that many cards, so the stacks aren't too big - if I were to have a very large collection, I'd have to sort them by discipline AND type of card to make finding the right card easier.

As for deck building, I usually make my deck on paper (or in ARDB) first, and then find the proper stacks of cards, take out the cards, sleeve them, and put the stacks back in the boxes I store them in.

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body:
I keep the vampires in binders: too many different cards in too few copies of each to be convenient to browse in a stack. 3 big binders are enough for all the vampires in the game if you put copies of the same vampire in the same slot. They are sorted by clan, then group, then capacity.

The library cards are in big stacks, sorted by type for generic cards or requirement (sect, clan, discipline, anarch, black hand), then alphabetically. That is quick enough to browse when searching for specific cards.

I always make a decklist on Secret Library before building the deck, so I never browse the cards randomly.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
I'm still thinking about how to sort my vampires. I store my library cards into drawers, sorted :
- by discipline
- multiple disciplines are apart (including 3-ways but not the bloodline disciplines cards with outferior)
- master
- event
- master skill cards
- master hunting grounds (could be mixed with masters though)
- disciplineless action (whatever their requirement)
- disciplineless reaction (whatever their requirement)
- disciplineless combat (whatever their requirement)
- disciplineless combo (whatever their requirement)
- disciplineless allies
- disciplineless retainers
- disciplineless equipment
- disciplineless political actions
- imbued related cards
Of course, inside a category everything is sorted alphabetically. For big collections (disciplineless actions, master cards...) I have some separators for each letter.

When building the deck, I use ARDB. When done, I pick up the cards.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand

I use this:

Vampires sorted alphabetically by clan, and then, by group, and then, by capacity, and then alphabetically.

Library cards are sorted in different stacks:
- No clan/trait/discipline requirement cards (splitted into Masters, Actions [plain actions, Equipment, Political Actions, Retainers], Action Modifiers, Combat, Reaction, Combo
- Discipline cards [Actions, Equipment / Retainer / Political, Action Modifiers, Reaction, Combo]
- Clan Cards (as above)
- Imbued cards (Conviction, Master, Action, ..)
- Weird stuff (Aye/Orun, Black Hand, Anarch, ...)

Messages.Author: Thargor
Messages.Body:
Inventory-wise, mine are all documented in Secret Library, which I use when deck-building.

Storage-wise, I have all vampires split up by clan (and each clan rubber-banded separately), and then each clan's vampires are alphabetised. Library cards are split up by type (Master, Actions, Combat, etc), then alphabetised and rubber-banded in groups by first-letter.

One thing to note about ARDB (that I didn't realise until I'd documented all of my collection at the time - thankfully it was a lot less cards than I now own) is that, unlike Secret Library, it matters which set each card comes from.

So, using WWEF as an example, in Secret Library I'd say I have 73 of them; in ARDB, I'd have to specify I have 22 HTTB, 6 LoB, 6 BH, 20 KMW, and so on. It's a lot more information to enter in, but I can see it being very useful if you have the patience to enter every card properly...
